suite.description: OrcaSAQ2 production speed settings versus ThinkingCap two-slot Q8 unified cache. Authored development regression suite; not held-out production data.

messages.content: Implement live(entries, now), returning a new dict of entries whose deadline is None or strictly greater than now. Values are (payload, deadline) tuples. Do not mutate input. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement order(deps). deps maps every node (strings) to its prerequisites. Include prerequisite-only nodes. Return a topological ordering, always choosing the alphabetically smallest currently ready node. Raise ValueError on a cycle. Do not mutate deps. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement merge(base, overlay): recursively merge dictionaries into a deep-independent result. Overlay values replace base values, including lists and None; a None value does not delete a key. Inputs are JSON-like dictionaries. Do not mutate or alias nested input data. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement coalesce(intervals): merge overlapping OR touching half-open integer intervals (start,end), discard empty intervals, raise ValueError if start>end. Return sorted tuples without mutating input. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

grader.tests:
a=[(5,8),(1,3),(3,5),(9,9)]
assert coalesce(a)==[(1,8)] and len(a)==4
assert coalesce([])==[]
assert coalesce([(1,9),(2,3),(10,11)])==[(1,9),(10,11)]
try: coalesce([(3,2)])
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError('backwards accepted')

messages.content: Implement delays(attempts, base, cap): a list of attempts-1 retry delays base*2**i capped at cap, i starts at zero. attempts includes the original request and must be >=1; base and cap must be >=0. Raise ValueError on invalid arguments. All inputs are integers. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement class LRU(capacity), capacity>=1 else ValueError. get(key) returns value or None and makes existing key most recently used. put(key,value) inserts/updates and evicts the least recently used key if over capacity. Keys and values are strings. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

grader.tests:
c=LRU(2)
c.put('a','1'); c.put('b','2')
assert c.get('a')=='1'
c.put('c','3')
assert c.get('b') is None
c.put('a','4'); c.put('d','5')
assert c.get('c') is None and c.get('a')=='4'
c=LRU(1); c.put('x','a'); c.put('x','b')
assert c.get('x')=='b'
try: LRU(0)
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError('bad capacity')

messages.content: Implement parse_jsonl(text): parse nonblank lines as JSON, returning values in order. Ignore whitespace-only lines. On invalid JSON raise ValueError whose message includes the one-based physical line number, counting blank lines. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement redact(value, sensitive), recursively copying JSON-like dictionaries/lists. Replace any dictionary value whose key case-insensitively matches a sensitive string with "[REDACTED]". Preserve unrelated scalars and do not mutate input. Sensitive matching is exact, not substring. Return only complete Python code using the standard library. The sensitive argument is a list of strings.

grader.tests:
a={'TOKEN':'abc','items':[{'password':'x','password_hint':'h'}],'n':3}
r=redact(a,['token','PASSWORD'])
assert r=={'TOKEN':'[REDACTED]','items':[{'password':'[REDACTED]','password_hint':'h'}],'n':3}
assert a['TOKEN']=='abc'
r['items'].append(4)
assert len(a['items'])==1
assert redact(None,['x']) is None

messages.content: Implement flatten(value), flattening nested dictionaries with string keys into dot-separated keys. Preserve lists and scalar leaves as values. Represent an empty dictionary leaf as {} at its path. An empty root produces {}. Keys never contain dots. Do not mutate input. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement rolling_sums(values,width), returning sums of each contiguous full window. width must be >=1 else ValueError. If width exceeds input length return []. Do not mutate values. Linear time required. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

grader.tests:
assert rolling_sums([1,-2,3,4],2)==[-1,1,7]
assert rolling_sums([],1)==[]
assert rolling_sums([2],2)==[]
assert rolling_sums([1,2],1)==[1,2]
assert rolling_sums([1,2],2)==[3]
try: rolling_sums([],0)
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError('width accepted')

messages.content: Implement paginate(items, after, limit). items is an already ascending list of distinct integer IDs. Return at most limit IDs strictly greater than after; after=None starts at the beginning. limit>=0 else ValueError. Do not mutate items. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

grader.tests:
assert paginate([1,3,5,8],3,2)==[5,8]
assert paginate([1,3,5],2,1)==[3]
assert paginate([1,3],None,0)==[]
assert paginate([1,3],None,1)==[1]
assert paginate([1,3],9,2)==[]
try: paginate([],None,-1)
except ValueError: pass
else: raise AssertionError('negative limit')

messages.content: Implement env_lines(text). Ignore blank lines and lines whose stripped form starts with #. Split other lines at the FIRST =, trim the key and value, preserve quotes and inline # literally. Duplicate keys use the last value. Empty keys or missing = raise ValueError. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement unique_latest(records). Each dict has string id and integer timestamp. Return one original record per ID: greatest timestamp wins, ties choose the last occurrence. Return records ordered by FIRST appearance of their IDs. Do not mutate input. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

grader.tests:
a=[{'id':'b','timestamp':2,'v':1},{'id':'a','timestamp':5},{'id':'b','timestamp':1},{'id':'b','timestamp':2,'v':9}]
assert unique_latest(a)==[a[3],a[1]]
assert len(a)==4
assert unique_latest([])==[]

messages.content: Implement histogram(edges, values): edges is a strictly increasing list with at least two numbers, otherwise ValueError. Count values in half-open bins [edge_i,edge_i+1); the final bin also includes the very last edge. Ignore out-of-range values. Return integer counts. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement normalize(path) for absolute POSIX-like paths. Reject non-absolute paths with ValueError. Collapse repeated /, ignore ., and resolve .. without going above root. Return / for root, and never a trailing slash elsewhere. No filesystem access. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement pack(items, max_bytes). items is a list of strings. Greedily pack consecutive items into lists whose sum of UTF-8 byte lengths is <=max_bytes. Do not split items, reorder, or count separators. max_bytes>=1 and every individual item must fit, otherwise ValueError. Empty input returns []; empty strings may share a full batch. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement reconcile(desired, actual), dictionaries from string name to JSON-like value. Return a dict with sorted name lists: create (only desired), update (both with unequal values), delete (only actual). Do not mutate inputs. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement admit(times, limit, window) for nondecreasing integer arrival times. Accept a request only if fewer than limit PREVIOUSLY ACCEPTED requests lie in (t-window,t]. Rejected requests do not count. Return booleans in arrival order. limit and window must be >=1 else ValueError. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

Implement frames(lines), where lines is a list of decoded SSE lines WITHOUT newline endings. Collect data: fields until a blank line; join their values with newline. Remove at most ONE space following the colon. Ignore comments and other fields. Return payload strings; discard a final event without its blank-line terminator. Return only complete Python code using the standard library. Skip events with no data fields; a data field with an empty value still produces an empty payload.

grader.tests:
assert frames([': ping','data: a','data: b','','data: tail'])==['a\nb']
assert frames(['data:  x','','data:','',''])==[' x','']
assert frames(['event: x',''])==[]
assert frames([])==[]

messages.content: Implement changed_paths(before,after) for JSON-like dict roots. Return sorted dot-separated paths for additions, removals, or unequal leaves. Recurse only where BOTH values are dictionaries; treat lists atomically. If an entire dictionary key is added/removed, return that parent path only. String keys never contain dots. Return only complete Python code using the standard library.

grader.tests:
assert changed_paths({'a':{'x':1,'y':2},'b':[1]},{'a':{'x':3,'y':2},'b':[2],'c':{'z':1}})==['a.x','b','c']
assert changed_paths({'a':{}},{})==['a']
assert changed_paths({'a':{}},{'a':None})==['a']
assert changed_paths({},{})==[]
